status.en: 19 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 30% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 19 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 30 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian forces have installed an interim administration in Tigray and are advancing toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging both Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. This adds the militia’s capture of the airport, reported Eritrean casualties, and the involvement of Secretary Rubio, which were not mentioned in the prior briefing.
summary.nb: Etiopiske styrker har installert en midlertidig administrasjon i Tigray og rykker frem mot den eritreiske grensen, mens en pro-regjeringsmilits sier at den har tatt kontroll over den regionale flyplassen og rapporterer at eritreiske styrker led tap der. USA, gjennom utenriksminister Marco Rubio, oppfordrer både Etiopia og Eritrea til å dempe kampene. Konflikten forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kampene i 2024, ifølge UCDP. Dette legger til militens erobring av flyplassen, rapporterte eritreiske tap og involveringen av minister Rubio, som ikke ble nevnt i den tidligere briefingen.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
